questions.question: The work done by a constant force of 5 Newton acting on a body is 5 joules. The displacement of the body in the direction of the applied force is _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The work done by a force is calculated using the formula: **Work = Force × Displacement**.
 
• Given the work done is 5 joules and the force applied is 5 Newtons.
 
• Rearranging the formula to find displacement: **Displacement = Work / Force**.
 
• Substituting the given values: **Displacement = 5 J / 5 N = 1 m**.
 
• Hence, the displacement in the direction of the applied force is **1 meter**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This theorem states that the work done by the net force on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.
 
• Mathematically, it is expressed as Work = ΔK.E.
 
 
 
• **Units of Work**
 
 
• The SI unit of work is the joule (J).
 
• 1 joule is defined as the work done when a force of 1 Newton displaces an object by 1 meter in the direction of the force.
 
 
 
• **Types of Forces**
 
 
• Forces can be categorized into various types such as gravitational force, normal force, frictional force, and applied force.
 
• In this context, the force mentioned is an applied force of 5 Newtons acting on the body.

options.text: The weight of a given object is 6 times higher on the moon as compared to its weight on the earth.

questions.solution:

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the gravitational force between the earth and the moon?

options.text: Gravitational force is repulsive when the moon is far from the earth.
Gravitational force is repulsive and minimum when the moon is far from the earth.
Gravitational force is attractive and maximum when the moon is close to the earth.
Gravitational force is attractive and maximum when the moon is far from the earth.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The gravitational force between two objects is always attractive in nature.
 
• The force of gravity is directly proportional to the product of the masses of the two objects involved.
 
• It is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the centers of the two objects.
 
• As the distance between the moon and the earth decreases, the gravitational force between them increases.
 
• When the moon is closest to the earth, the gravitational force is at its maximum value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inverse Square Law**

 
 
• The gravitational force follows the inverse square law, meaning it decreases with the square of the distance between the two objects.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**
 
 
• This law states that every point mass attracts every other point mass by a force acting along the line intersecting both points.
 
 
 
• **Tidal Forces**
 
 
• The gravitational attraction between the earth and moon causes tidal forces, which are responsible for the ocean tides on earth.

questions.question: The gravitational force between two objects of masses m₁ and m₂ is directly proportional to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**m₁ × m₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The gravitational force between two objects is governed by Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation.
 
• The formula for gravitational force is F = G * (m₁ * m₂) / r², where G is the gravitational constant.
 
• The force is directly proportional to the product of the masses of the two objects (m₁ and m₂).
 
• This means that if either mass increases, the gravitational force between them also increases.
 
• The gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the centers of the two masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational Constant (G)**

 
 
• G is a universal constant with a value of approximately 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N(m/kg)².
 
 
 
• It is a key component in the formula for calculating gravitational force.
 
• **Inverse Square Law**
 
 
• This law states that the force between two masses is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• This means that if the distance is doubled, the gravitational force becomes one-fourth.
 
 
 
• **Mass and Weight**
 
 
• Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and is usually measured in kilograms.
 
• Weight is the force exerted by gravity on an object and is dependent on both the mass of the object and the gravitational field strength.
 
• Weight can be calculated using the formula Weight = Mass × Gravitational field strength.

__
 
• This law states that every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• **Key Formula:** F = G (m₁ m₂)/(r²) where:
 
 
• **G** is the gravitational constant (6 × 10⁻¹¹ Nm²kg⁻²),
 
• **m_1** and **m_2** are the masses of the two objects,
 
• **r** is the distance between the centers of the two masses.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Force (F)** is measured in Newtons (N).
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** [M¹L³T⁻²].

**Calculation:**__

Given data:

Gravitational Constant, **G** = 6 × 10⁻¹¹ Nm²kg⁻²

Mass of the Earth, **M** = 6 × 10²⁴ kg

Mass of the Moon, **m** = 8 × 10²² kg

Distance between Earth and Moon, **r** = 4 × 10⁸ m

F = G (Mm)/(r²)

⇒ F = 6 times 10⁻¹¹ frac{6 times 10²⁴ times 8 times 10²²}{(4 times 10⁸)²}

⇒ F = 6 times 10⁻¹¹ times 3 times 10³⁰ = 1.8 times 10²⁰ N

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT increase the rate of evaporation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decrease in temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Evaporation is the process by which water changes from a liquid to a gas or vapor.
 
• An increase in temperature generally increases the rate of evaporation because the molecules move faster and are more likely to escape into the air.
 
• An increase in surface area allows more molecules to evaporate at once, thus increasing the rate of evaporation.
 
• An increase in wind speed removes the air saturated with water vapor from the vicinity, allowing more water to evaporate.
 
• A decrease in humidity means the air can hold more water vapor, thus increasing the rate of evaporation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Condensation**

 
 
• Condensation is the process by which water vapor in the air is changed into liquid water.
 
• It is the opposite of evaporation and occurs when the air is cooled to its dew point.
 
 
 
• **Boiling**
 
 
• Boiling is the rapid vaporization of a liquid, which occurs when a liquid is heated to its boiling point.
 
• At this temperature, the vapor pressure of the liquid is equal to the external pressure exerted on the liquid.
 
 
 
• **Sublimation**
 
 
• Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas phase without passing through the liquid phase.
 
• This occurs under specific conditions of pressure and temperature.

questions.question: In which of the following phenomena does a solid substance change into a liquid substance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fusion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fusion is the process where a solid substance changes into a liquid substance.
 
• This process occurs when the temperature of the solid reaches its melting point.
 
• During fusion, the solid absorbs heat energy, which breaks the intermolecular bonds holding its molecules in place.
 
• The absorbed heat energy increases the kinetic energy of the molecules, causing them to move more freely and transition into the liquid state.
 
• Examples of fusion include the melting of ice into water and the melting of metals when heated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solidification**

 
 
• This is the process where a liquid changes into a solid, also known as freezing.
 
• It occurs when the temperature of a liquid is lowered below its freezing point.
 
 
 
• **Sublimation**
 
 
• Sublimation is the process where a solid changes directly into a gas without passing through the liquid state.
 
• An example of sublimation is dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) changing directly into carbon dioxide gas.
 
 
 
• **Deposition**
 
 
• Deposition is the process where a gas changes directly into a solid without becoming a liquid first.
 
• An example of deposition is the formation of frost on cold surfaces.

questions.question: When an empty bottle is closed air tight and pushed inside water it bounces back when it is released. This is because ________.

options.text: water does not exert force on an empty bottle
gravitational force on a bottle is equal to the buoyant force of the water
upthrust of water on a bottle is greater than the gravitational force acting on the bottle
gravitational force acting on the bottle is greater than the upthrust of water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**upthrust of water on a bottle is greater than the gravitational force acting on the bottle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an empty bottle is pushed underwater, it displaces a volume of water equal to its own volume.
 
• The water exerts an upward buoyant force on the bottle, known as upthrust.
 
• Since the bottle is empty (filled with air), its density is much lower than the density of water.
 
• The upthrust exerted by the water is greater than the gravitational force acting on the empty bottle.
 
• This difference in forces causes the bottle to bounce back to the surface when it is released.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buoyant Force**

 
 
• It is the upward force exerted by a fluid on an object submerged in it.
 
• The magnitude of the buoyant force is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.
 
 
 
• **Archimedes' Principle**
 
 
• This principle states that any object submerged in a fluid experiences a buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces.
 
• It explains why objects float or sink in fluids.
 
 
 
• **Density**
 
 
• Density is defined as mass per unit volume of a substance.
 
• Objects with lower density than the fluid they are in will float, while those with higher density will sink.

questions.question: Which of the following physical quantities represents the rate of change of velocity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate of change of velocity of an object with respect to time.
 
• It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• The SI unit of acceleration is meters per second squared (m/s²).
 
• Acceleration can be caused by changing the speed of an object, its direction of motion, or both.
 
• In mathematical terms, acceleration is the derivative of velocity with respect to time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed**

 
 
• Speed is a scalar quantity that refers to how fast an object is moving, regardless of its direction.
 
• It is calculated as the distance traveled per unit of time.
 
 
 
• **Velocity**
 
 
• Velocity is a vector quantity that describes the speed of an object in a specific direction.
 
• It is calculated as the displacement per unit of time.
 
 
 
• **Distance**
 
 
• Distance is a scalar quantity that refers to the total path length covered by an object during its motion.
 
• It does not take the direction of motion into account.

questions.question: The relation between thrust (T), pressure (P) and area (A) of an object in a given medium is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: T = P x A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Thrust (T) is a force exerted by the pressure (P) acting over a specific area (A).
 
• The formula for thrust is given by the product of pressure and area: T = P x A.
 
• This relationship indicates that thrust increases with an increase in either pressure or area.
 
• Pressure is defined as the force per unit area, and when multiplied by area, it gives the total force or thrust.
 
• Understanding this relationship is crucial in fields such as fluid dynamics and aerodynamics, where pressure and thrust play a significant role.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fluid Dynamics**

 
 
• It is the study of the movement of liquids and gases and their interactions with solid boundaries.
 
• Understanding the principles of fluid dynamics is essential for designing efficient systems in engineering and natural sciences.
 
 
 
• **Aerodynamics**
 
 
• Aerodynamics is the study of the behavior of air as it interacts with solid objects, such as an aircraft wing.
 
• It involves the application of fluid dynamics principles to understand and predict the forces and moments acting on bodies in motion through the air.
 
 
 
• **Pressure Measurement**
 
 
• Pressure is measured using instruments like manometers, barometers, and pressure transducers.
 
• Accurate measurement of pressure is vital in various industrial and scientific applications to ensure system efficiency and safety.

questions.question: A cubic wooden block of side 2 m is lying on a tabletop. If the mass of the wooden block is 10 kg, then the pressure exerted by the wooden block on the tabletop is: (consider g = 10 m/s²)

__**Concept:**__

**Pressure:**

__
 
• Pressure is defined as the force applied per unit area.
 
• Formula: P = (F)/(A)
 
• Here, **Force (F)** is the weight of the wooden block, which is the product of mass (m) and acceleration due to gravity (g).
 
• Weight (W) = m × g
 
• **SI unit:** Pascal (Pa) or N/m²
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]

**Calculation:**__

__
 
• **Ohm's Law** is one of the fundamental principles in **electricity and electronics.**
 
• It establishes a direct relationship between **voltage (V), current (I),** and **resistance (R)** in an electrical circuit.
 
• The law is mathematically expressed as: **V = I × R**, where:
 
 
• **V** is the voltage in volts.
 
• **I** is the current in amperes.
 
• **R** is the resistance in ohms.
 
 
 
• Ohm's Law implies that if the resistance in a circuit is constant, the **voltage and current** are directly proportional to each other.
 
• This relationship helps in determining unknown quantities when any two parameters (voltage, current, or resistance) are known.
 
• It is widely used in the design and analysis of **electrical circuits** and is a fundamental concept in **physics and engineering.**
 
• Ohm's Law is applicable to **linear circuits**, where the resistance remains constant regardless of the voltage or current.

 __

 __

• Although resistance is a factor in power calculations, this is not the primary relationship outlined by **Ohm's Law.**

• However, this relationship involves power and does not directly represent the fundamental principle of **Ohm's Law.**

questions.question: A speeding vehicle can skid on the bend of the road because of _____________.

The Correct answer is __**Centrifugal Force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Centrifugal force** is a pseudo force that acts outward on a body moving in a circular path.
 
• It is caused due to the **inertia of motion** of the object as it resists the change in direction while moving around a curve.
 
• When a vehicle moves at a high speed and takes a turn, the **centrifugal force** pushes the vehicle outward, away from the center of the curve.
 
• At higher speeds, the force increases significantly, and if the road is slippery or the friction is insufficient, the vehicle can skid due to the overpowering outward force.
 
• **Centrifugal force** is proportional to the square of the velocity of the vehicle and inversely proportional to the radius of the curve.
 
• Effective road design, such as banking of curves, helps counteract the effects of this force to prevent skidding.
 
• This phenomenon is crucial in vehicle dynamics and is considered while designing roadways and racetracks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gravitational Force**__

 __
 
• **Gravitational force** is the natural force of attraction between two masses, such as the Earth and objects on its surface.
 
• It does not play a direct role in causing skidding on a bend but contributes to keeping the vehicle grounded.
 
• Examples include the force responsible for the weight of objects and the motion of planets around the Sun.
 
 
 
• **Centripetal Force**__
 __
 
• **Centripetal force** is the force directed towards the center of the circular path that keeps the vehicle in motion along the curve.
 
• It works in opposition to the outward **centrifugal force** and ensures the object does not move tangentially to the curve.
 
• Examples include the tension in a string when swinging an object in a circle.
 
 
 
• **Frictional Force**__
 
 
• **Frictional force** is the force that resists the relative motion between two surfaces in contact.
 
• It provides the necessary grip for vehicles to take turns without skidding.
 
• Examples include the traction between tires and the road surface.

• Hydraulic systems like brakes, lifts, and presses function based on Pascal's law by transmitting applied force through an incompressible fluid.
 
• In hydraulic brakes, a small force applied at the brake pedal gets amplified by transmitting pressure through brake fluid to stop the vehicle effectively.
 
• Hydraulic lifts use Pascal's principle to lift heavy loads by applying force over a smaller area, which is then transmitted to a larger area.
 
• This principle is widely used in industries and machinery for efficient force multiplication.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pascal's Law Formula:**

 
 
• The formula is given by: **P = F/A**, where P is the pressure, F is the force applied, and A is the area.
 
• This equation explains how force is transmitted through a fluid in hydraulic systems.
 
 
 
• **Incompressible Fluid:**
 
 
• An incompressible fluid is a fluid whose density does not change significantly under pressure.
 
• Hydraulic systems rely on such fluids for effective force transmission.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Pascal's Law:**
 
 
• Hydraulic brakes in vehicles, where force from the brake pedal is transmitted to brake pads.
 
• Hydraulic lifts used in construction and automotive industries to lift heavy objects.
 
• Hydraulic presses used for shaping, compressing, or molding materials.
 
 
 
• **Hydraulic Multiplier Effect:**
 
 
• Pascal's law enables a small force applied over a small area to generate a larger force over a larger area.
 
• This principle is what makes hydraulic systems highly efficient for heavy-duty applications.

questions.question: Hooke's law establishes the relationship between which two physical quantities in elastic materials?

• Stress refers to the force per unit area applied to a material, while strain is the relative deformation or change in shape/size of the material.
 
• Hooke's law applies only within the elastic limit, beyond which permanent deformation occurs.

• **Stress Types:** Stress can be classified as tensile, compressive, or shear based on the direction of the applied force.
 
• **Applications:** Hooke's law is widely applied in designing springs, calculating material properties, and analyzing mechanical systems.
 
• **Limitations:** Hooke's law is valid only for elastic materials and does not account for plastic deformation or non-linear stress-strain behavior.

questions.question: Which radiation is emitted when a stream of accelerating electrons strikes a metal target?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**X-ray**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a stream of **accelerating electrons** strikes a metal target, **X-rays** are produced. This phenomenon occurs due to the sudden deceleration of electrons when they collide with the target material.
 
• X-rays are a form of **electromagnetic radiation** with a wavelength shorter than ultraviolet rays but longer than gamma rays.
 
• The process of X-ray production involves two primary mechanisms:
 
 
• **Bremsstrahlung Radiation:** This occurs when electrons are decelerated upon interaction with the atomic nuclei of the target material, releasing energy in the form of X-rays.
 
• **Characteristic X-rays:** These are emitted when electrons in the target material's inner shells are ejected, and electrons from higher energy levels transition to fill the vacancies.
 
 
 
• The metal target used in the production of X-rays is typically made of **tungsten** or similar materials due to their high atomic number and melting points.
 
• X-rays are widely used in **medical imaging**, such as in X-ray radiography, CT scans, and cancer treatments like radiotherapy.
 
• They are also crucial in **scientific research** (e.g., X-ray crystallography) and industrial applications like material testing.
 
• The discovery of X-rays is credited to **Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen** in **1895**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gamma-ray**__

 __
 
• **Gamma-rays** are the highest energy form of electromagnetic radiation, having the shortest wavelength and highest frequency.
 
• They are typically produced during the **nuclear decay** of radioactive isotopes or in high-energy astrophysical processes.
 
• Gamma-rays are used in **radiotherapy** for cancer treatment and in **industrial radiography** to inspect metal parts and welds for defects.
 
 
 
• **Cathode ray**__
 __
 
• **Cathode rays** are streams of **electrons** emitted from the cathode in a vacuum tube when a high voltage is applied.
 
• They are not electromagnetic radiation but rather a physical stream of particles.
 
• Cathode rays are used in **cathode-ray tubes (CRTs)**, which were historically used in televisions and computer monitors.
 
 
 
• **Alpha-ray**__
 
 
• **Alpha-rays** consist of **helium nuclei** (two protons and two neutrons) emitted during the radioactive decay of heavy elements like uranium or radium.
 
• They are not electromagnetic radiation but rather particulate radiation.
 
• Alpha particles have a **low penetration power** and are stopped by a sheet of paper or human skin.

questions.question: Which type of wall is present in the closed system?

• **Heat energy**
 
 between the system and surroundings.
 
• Examples of closed systems include:
 
 
• A sealed pressure cooker before the whistle blows
 
• A gas enclosed in a piston-cylinder arrangement

• **Thermal equilibrium**
 
 between systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When two resistors are connected in series, the total resistance is the sum of their individual resistances.
 
• If each resistor has a resistance of R, the total resistance is calculated as R + R.
 
• Therefore, the total resistance when two equal resistors are connected in series is 2R.
 
• This principle is derived from Ohm's Law, which states that the total resistance in a series circuit is the sum of the individual resistances.
 
• Series circuits have only one path for current flow, causing the resistances to add up.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:**

 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
 
 
• **Series Circuit:**
 
 
• A series circuit is one in which components are connected end-to-end so that the current has only one path to take through the circuit.
 
• If any component in a series circuit fails, the entire circuit is broken and current stops flowing.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Circuit:**
 
 
• A parallel circuit is one in which components are connected across common points or junctions, providing multiple paths for the current.
 
• The total resistance of a parallel circuit is found by the reciprocal of the sum of the reciprocals of each individual resistance.
 
 
 
• **Resistor:**
 
 
• A resistor is a passive electrical component with two terminals that implements electrical resistance as a circuit element.
 
• They are used to reduce current flow, adjust signal levels, divide voltages, bias active elements, and terminate transmission lines, among other uses.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct with regard to resistances in a series circuit?

options.text: Total resistance is less than any individual resistance.
Total resistance is equal to the product of all resistances.
Total resistance is inversely proportional to each resistance.
Total resistance is equal to the sum of all individual resistances.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Total resistance is equal to the sum of all individual resistances.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a series circuit, the total resistance (Rₜₒₜₐₗ) is the sum of all individual resistances (R₁, R₂, R₃, etc.).
 
• The formula to calculate total resistance in a series circuit is: Rₜₒₜₐₗ = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + ...
 
• This means that the more resistors you add to the series circuit, the higher the total resistance becomes.
 
• Unlike parallel circuits, in a series circuit, the current has only one path to travel, thus the total resistance is simply the additive sum of all resistances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:**

 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current (I) through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage (V) across the two points and inversely proportional to the resistance (R).
 
• The formula is V = I * R.
 
 
 
• **Series Circuit Characteristics:**
 
 
• In a series circuit, the same current flows through all components.
 
• If one component fails, the entire circuit is interrupted.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Circuit:**
 
 
• In a parallel circuit, the voltage across each component is the same.
 
• The total resistance is less than the smallest individual resistance.
 
• The formula for total resistance in a parallel circuit is 1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ + ...
 
 
 
• **Applications of Series Circuits:**
 
 
• Series circuits are commonly used in applications where the operation of the circuit depends on each component functioning correctly, such as in string lights.
 
• They are also used in voltage divider circuits.

questions.question: What is the relationship between current (I), power (P), and voltage (V)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I = P ÷ V**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The relationship between current (I), power (P), and voltage (V) is defined by the formula **I = P ÷ V**.
 
• This formula is derived from the basic electrical power equation **P = V × I**, where P is power in watts, V is voltage in volts, and I is current in amperes.
 
• To find the current, you rearrange the formula to I = P ÷ V, which means the current is equal to the power divided by the voltage.
 
• This relationship is fundamental in electrical engineering and is used to calculate one quantity if the other two are known.
 
• The formula applies to both DC (Direct Current) and AC (Alternating Current) circuits, although for AC circuits, power calculations also involve the power factor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law**

 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current flowing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is V = I × R, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• This law is fundamental in understanding electrical circuits and is used alongside the power formula.
 
 
 
• **Power Factor**
 
 
• In AC circuits, the power factor is the ratio of real power used to do work to the apparent power flowing in the circuit.
 
• A power factor of 1 indicates that all the power is being effectively converted into work, while a power factor less than 1 indicates some power is wasted.
 
• Power factor is important in the design and analysis of AC electrical power systems.
 
 
 
• **Types of Current**
 
 
• **Direct Current (DC)**: The flow of electric charge is only in one direction.
 
• **Alternating Current (AC)**: The flow of electric charge periodically reverses direction.
 
• Most household electrical systems use AC because it is more efficient for long-distance transmission.
 
 
 
• **Electrical Power**
 
 
• Electrical power is the rate at which electrical energy is transferred by an electric circuit.
 
• The SI unit of power is the watt (W), which is equivalent to one joule per second.
 
• Power can be calculated using the formula P = V × I for both DC and AC circuits, with adjustments for power factor in AC circuits.
